A1.justification: Despite the changed title and broader scope, both PDFs describe the same conformal C2ST work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison and matching of retained material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results for perturbed Gaussian posteriors, classifier degradation, calibration-size ablations, and high-dimensional manifold posteriors.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and adds CIFAR-10 corruption experiments and a galaxy-based gravitational-lensing evaluation.

M1.justification: The Uniform test still uses independent calibration sets followed by a KS test, and the Multiple test retains its shared-calibration statistic and variance estimator. The expanded theory and experiment-specific classifiers do not establish a change to the proposed testing procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-10 blur, swirl, and noise detection and a PROBES-based gravitational-lensing inverse problem (Sections 5.2–5.3). The Gaussian perturbations and high-dimensional manifold experiment remain. Mean shift and mode collapse were already evaluated in v1; their changed placement is not new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated Discriminative Calibration, AutoML, and MMDFuse comparisons to the Gaussian benchmark plots, alongside retained C2ST, SBC, and TARP baselines. These methods also appear in the new lensing comparison. Local C2ST is discussed but explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E3.justification: The Gaussian comparison panels switch from Conformal Uniform(200) to Uniform(50), although the broader calibration-size sweep remains. New protocols include image classification using frozen Inception features and 1,024 training images per source, and lensing experiments using 2,000 training samples per source with diffusion-score bias interpolation. These are substantial additions to the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 extends the robustness investigation to strong versus weak image classifiers and a lensing classifier-degradation sweep at fixed posterior bias (Figure 3 and Table 2b). These test whether robustness transfers beyond the original synthetic settings. The existing calibration-size ablations and Gaussian/manifold degradation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed averaging remains unchanged. v2 adds reporting of 50 lensing replicates, a default of 64 image-evaluation replicates, and 100 bootstrap resamples for Discriminative Calibration. It does not establish increased repetitions for the retained Gaussian experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds image and lensing outcomes and revises Gaussian comparison curves, including markedly lower plotted SBC/TARP power. New Table 2a reports 66% power for Uniform(50), 50% for Multiple, and 28% for C2ST at bias γ=0.60 and degradation β=0. The Gaussian Uniform comparisons also change calibration budget, so those differences are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The original Uniform-test robustness bound is retained, but v2 adds a conditional p-value variance lemma, a rare-ties assumption, and Theorem 4.2 on the Multiple statistic's oracle scaling and relative estimation-error gap. Appendix A.4 expands into Hoeffding decomposition, central-limit, tie-noise, null-validity, and robustness derivations.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and new conclusion broaden the contribution from neural posterior validation to general two-sample testing. v2 also elevates the budget-matched Multiple test from an alternative comparator to a central contribution with its own robustness claim, alongside the retained Uniform test.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit M-closed versus M-open and global versus local applicability limits, distinguishes Uniform's finite-sample guarantee from Multiple's asymptotic validity, and discusses when Multiple outperforms Uniform. Appendix D adds practical guidance and failure conditions, although its language about certifying joint validity overstates what non-rejection establishes.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation through CIFAR preprocessing, classifier architecture, optimization, corruption grids, DC settings, and method-specific sampling budgets. However, v1's explicit Gaussian observation distribution and covariance construction are omitted. The code-access link is retained rather than newly provided.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning within classifier and kernel two-sample testing, adding discussion of DC, AutoML, MMDFuse, local C2ST, and earlier classifier-test theory. It also qualifies the SBC comparison using newer test quantities and relates its assumptions to ranking and margin-condition literature, beyond v1's narrower posterior-validation positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and results narrative are extensively rewritten around general two-sample testing. The original unified methods section is reorganized into separate preliminaries, Uniform, and Multiple sections; Gaussian descriptions move to the appendix, and a conclusion and practitioner guide are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. v2 adds an image-results figure and tables for sampling budgets, lensing results, and corruption grids, while expanding Gaussian plot legends and comparator curves. Mean shift replaces mode collapse in the main figure; both remain in the appendix, and many existing plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's limited empirical scope and comparator coverage through image and galaxy-based inverse-problem evaluations and broader baseline comparisons. Explicit sampling budgets and clearer applicability and validity limits substantially improve readers' ability to assess the methods. Some Gaussian reproducibility details are lost, and the practitioner guide overstates what non-rejection certifies, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial strengthening of the comparative evidence and practical explanation.
